data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note summarizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for Hungary, covering adults aged 16–65 assessed in 2022–23 across three domains: literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving. Proficiency is reported on 500-point scales and mapped to discrete proficiency levels, with uncertainty shown via 95% confidence intervals. Hungary’s mean performance is below the OECD average in all three domains (literacy 248, numeracy 254, adaptive problem solving 241), and relatively large shares of adults are at or below Level 1 (literacy 32%, numeracy 29%, adaptive problem solving 37%). The note also reports descriptive subgroup differences (e.g., older adults 55–65 scoring lower than 25–34 year-olds) and trends over time between 2017–18 and 2022–23, including declines in literacy and numeracy and increased low performance. It further links skills to economic and social outcomes using reported associations (e.g., numeracy and labour force participation; numeracy and wages), but the excerpt does not provide the underlying modeling specifications, PV handling, or missing-data procedures.
